facts: The paper presents a method for blind estimation of reverberation times in reverberant enclosures.
The proposed algorithm is based on a statistical model.
The statistical model is of short-term log-energy sequences.
The statistical model is for echo-free speech.
The proposed algorithm computes a Maximum Likelihood estimate of the room full-band reverberation time.
The proposed algorithm takes as input a speech utterance recorded in a reverberant room.
The estimation method is shown to require little data.
The estimation method is shown to perform satisfactorily.
The method has been successfully applied to robust automatic speech recognition in reverberant environments by model selection.
For the automatic speech recognition application, the reverberation time is first estimated from the reverberated speech utterance to be recognized.
The estimation is then used to select the best acoustic model.
The best acoustic model is selected out of a library of models trained in various artificial re-verberant conditions.
The library of models is trained in various artificial re-verberant conditions.
Speech recognition experiments in simulated and real reverberant environments show the efficiency of the approach.
The approach outperforms standard channel normalization techniques.
entities: statistical model of short-term log-energy sequences
Maximum Likelihood estimate of the room full-band reverberation time
